text: A portable Hydrogen Small Unit Power (H-SUP) system prototype has been developed by the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory to function as a fuel cell electric generator able to support remote field operations where low detectability is critical (Pasquini 2025). The fuel cell has previously been successfully demonstrated for unmanned vehicle applications in the Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division’s H2 Stalker Program, with power-to-weight advantages. • U.S. manufacturer NovaSpark Energy Corp. offers designs for hydrogen generators as closed-loop systems that can be transported on military trailers and that function in low- humidity desert environments or Indo-Pacific islands (Kauffman 2025). E.8 Advanced Fuel Cell Technology Advanced fuel cell technologies offer improved efficiencies for electricity generation based on chemical conversion to electricity compared to traditional combustion-based conversion (DOE HFTO n.d.-a.). Researchers continue to address technological challenges to improve the cost, performance, and durability of fuel cells both for mobile and stationary power applications (DOE HFTO n.d.-a, NLR 2025b). One notable advancement area is hydrogen, which can be used to generate electricity for stationary applications, with one key advantage being its ability to be stored for long periods. When paired with salt cavern storage and fuel cell electricity generation, hydrogen can be competitive with today’s natural gas combined-cycle technologies (Hunter et al. 2021). An advanced fuel cell on the verge of commercialization includes Japan-based Honda’s Next Generation Fuel Cell Module planned for 2027 (Honda 2025), which is slated to deliver three times the power density of previous models (Tripathi 2025). The fuel cell features a compact design, measuring 28.7 by 27.5 by 22.8 inches; and the device operates effectively across a wide range of conditions, with temperatures ranging from -30°C (-22°F) to +60°C (140°F) and at altitudes up to 11,500 feet. Additionally, in 2026, Honda is scheduled to begin production on its fuel cell power generator (Honda 2025), which is designed as a reliable backup power source for large-scale facilities, with a unit capacity up to 250 kW of power and multiple connected units providing 1,000 kW or more (Tripathi 2025). 79 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Some emerging research offers the potential for innovative options for expanded applications. An advanced proton exchange membrane fuel cell for application in underwater EVs (autonomous underwater vehicles) is at the prototype stage, developed by German researchers, it uses artificial gills to overcome pressure challenges for this oxygen-based technology (Lea 2025; Merckelbach and Georgopanos 2025). 80 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Appendix F. Small Modular Reactors Small modular reactors (SMRs) are an emerging technology that will offer an advanced option for energy generation as well as heat generation, hydrogen production, and desalination for potable water (IAEA 2024; INL 2025). These small nuclear reactors can generate up to approximately 300 MW(e) (or 7.2 million kWh) per day (European Commission, n.d.-a, n.d.-b).
